2D pixel-art multi-agent visualizer: Vite/React/Three.js/TypeScript frontend; FastAPI/LangGraph/Pydantic backend; optional Tauri. All agents work on codebase. Prefix session with [Council Role: Architect], [Council Role: Analyst], [Council Role: Implementer], or [Council Role: Reviewer]; roles coordinate fungible generalists.

Project: `<REDACTED_USERPATH>/agent-marketplace-demo/`; `src/components/`, `src/hooks/`, `agent-backend/agents/`, `agent-backend/models/`, `agent-backend/sprites/`.

ALWAYS use `bd` (beads) from this project directory:
cd <REDACTED_USERPATH>/agent-marketplace-demo
Always check your Agent Mail for coordination.
cd <REDACTED_USERPATH>/agent-marketplace-demo
bv --robot-triage
bv --robot-next
bv --robot-plan
bv --robot-insights | jq '.Cycles'
bv --robot-insights | jq '.bottlenecks'
**CRITICAL:** Never run bare `bv` — it launches interactive TUI that blocks.
Before editing files, reserve them:
file_reservation_paths \
project_key="<REDACTED_USERPATH>/agent-marketplace-demo" \
agent_name="YourAgentName" \
paths=["src/components/AgentCanvas.tsx"] \
After completing work:
release_file_reservations \
project_key="<REDACTED_USERPATH>/agent-marketplace-demo" \
agent_name="YourAgentName"

1. Read this AGENTS.md file carefully
2. Read README.md
3. Register with Agent Mail
4. Introduce yourself to other agents
5. Check inbox for messages
cd <REDACTED_USERPATH>/agent-marketplace-demo
bv --robot-next
Pick useful bead. Send Agent Mail with Subject: `[bd-XXX] Starting task description`; Thread ID: `bd-XXX`; mention reserved files. Mark bead `in_progress`. Implement with strict TypeScript, hooks, instancing, Python type hints/Pydantic. Fresh-eyes review new code and fix issues repeatedly; use ultrathink. Update bead `done`, release reservations, send `[bd-XXX] Completed`, respond to messages. Periodically deeply review/fix others’ code. After logical work, commit all changed files in logical groups with detailed messages, then push. Don't edit the code at all. Don't commit obviously ephemeral files. Use ultrathink.

Use strict TypeScript (no `any`)
Functional components with hooks
React Three Fiber for Three.js integration
`useFrame` hook for animations
`useThree` hook for Three.js access
shadcn/ui for UI components
Use `InstancedMesh` for 100+ identical sprites
Sprite sheets for animations
LOD (Level of Detail) for performance
Frustum culling (automatic in Three.js)
Pixel-perfect rendering: `renderer.setPixelRatio(1, 1)`
Use FastAPI for async API
Pydantic for request/response validation
LangGraph for agent orchestration
Type hints everywhere
Async/await for I/O operations
State graph with nodes: `perceive`, `reason`, `act`
TypedDict for state
LLM via LangChain OpenAI
Batch processing for multiple agents
**No `any` types** - Use proper TypeScript types
**No `console.log`** - Use proper logging
**No hardcoded values** - Use constants/config
**Type safety everywhere** - Python type hints + Pydantic
**Error handling** - Try/catch, proper error messages
**Performance** - Profile before optimizing
**Tests** - Write tests for critical paths
[Component] Brief description
Related beads: bd-XXX, bd-YYY
1. **Always work from `<REDACTED_USERPATH>/agent-marketplace-demo/`**
2. **Always reserve files before editing**
3. **Always check Agent Mail between tasks**
4. **Always self-review before marking bead done**
5. **Always communicate what you're working on**
6. **Never skip quality checks**

If beads don't exist yet, create them for: bd-001 Tauri/React/TypeScript; bd-002 Three.js/R3F; bd-003 shadcn/ui; bd-004 FastAPI; bd-005 LangGraph; bd-006 pixel sprites; bd-007 render agent; bd-008 click detection; bd-009 detail panel; bd-010 frontend/backend connection.

**Remember:** Every agent is fungible. Just start working and coordinate via Agent Mail!
**When ending a work session**, you MUST complete ALL steps below. Work is NOT complete until `git push` succeeds.
1. **File issues for remaining work** - Create issues for anything that needs follow-up
2. **Run quality gates** (if code changed) - Tests, linters, builds
3. **Update issue status** - Close finished work, update in-progress items
4. **PUSH TO REMOTE** - This is MANDATORY:
git pull --rebase
git status  # MUST show "up to date with origin"
5. **Clean up** - Clear stashes, prune remote branches
6. **Verify** - All changes committed AND pushed
7. **Hand off** - Provide context for next session
Work is NOT complete until `git push` succeeds
NEVER stop before pushing - that leaves work stranded locally
NEVER say "ready to push when you are" - YOU must push
If push fails, resolve and retry until it succeeds
